answer: To keep cheap clones from flooding votes, every new agent must pass a velvet-rope admission: it locks a slashable bond into a hollow escrow that cannot vote or earn until independent attestors score a rolling window of its unique work. Only when that quality curve hits a published zenith—ten distinct counterparties and no overlapping key material or reused task hashes—does the escrow convert into voting weight. If two identities share a work fingerprint, both bonds in the hollow escrow are slashed, so spinning clones never reaches the zenith and cannot multiply influence.
